Prologue · 序

One gate. One viewpoint.
One hundred years.

Taipei's North Gate, officially Cheng'en Gate (承恩門), was completed in 1884 as part of the Qing-era city walls. Of the city's five gates, it is the only one that still keeps its original appearance.

The four images that follow were generated with AI from the same fixed viewpoint. The gate stays at the center of every frame, so the only thing that changes is the city around it: its streets, vehicles, signs and people. Scroll down to travel from the 1920s to the 2020s.

1920s

Chapter I · 日治時期

1920sColonial Taipei

After Taiwan came under Japanese rule in 1895, the colonial government began tearing down Taipei's city walls in 1900 and built broad boulevards on their foundations. The North Gate survived and was left standing on its own in the middle of the new road.

By the 1920s, the area around it had become a showcase of colonial modernity, with Western-style banks, trading companies and post offices lining wide, unpaved streets.

Look closer

Rickshaws, bicycles and handcarts share the road. People in kimono and Western suits pass under Japanese flags and vertical shop signs. The real Beimen Post Office, completed in 1930, still stands across from the gate today.

AI-generated reconstruction · North Gate, Taipei

1950s

Chapter II · 戰後

1950sPostwar Taipei

Japanese rule ended in 1945. In 1949, the government of the Republic of China relocated to Taipei, bringing a sudden wave of new residents from mainland China.

Shop signs switched to Chinese names, and the streets near the gate filled with small shops, bicycles, trucks and the first private cars. Housing was scarce, and the city began to spread far beyond the line of its old walls.

Look closer

Bicycles are now the main way to get around, and the signs for department stores and trading houses are written in Chinese. The gate itself is unchanged, a quiet constant in a city that had just changed hands.

AI-generated reconstruction · North Gate, Taipei

1990s

Chapter III · 快速都市化

1990sModernizing Taipei

By the 1990s, Taipei was one of Asia's most crowded cities. Taxis, buses and scooters filled every lane, and roads were lifted into the air to keep traffic moving. In 1977, the approach ramp of the Zhongxiao Bridge was built around the North Gate, passing less than a meter from it and hiding the gate behind concrete for almost four decades.

New infrastructure was also reshaping the city: the railway went underground when the new Taipei Main Station opened in 1989, and the first MRT line opened in 1996.

Look closer

Billboards for banks, airlines and insurance companies crowd the skyline, and the bus is headed for Guanghua Market and Taipei Main Station. Notice what the AI left out: the elevated ramp that really wrapped around the gate in these years does not appear in the image.

AI-generated reconstruction · North Gate, Taipei

2020s

Chapter IV · 重新發現

2020sRediscovering Taipei

In February 2016, the Zhongxiao Bridge ramp was torn down, and the North Gate stood in the open again. The space around it became North Gate Square, which opened in 2017.

Nearby heritage buildings were restored as well. The former Railway Department reopened in 2020 as a museum park of the National Taiwan Museum, and the old Mitsui & Co. office was moved and reopened as a small museum.

Look closer

Traffic has moved to the edges, and people can walk right up to the gate, something that was impossible for most of the late 20th century. A century after the walls came down, the gate is no longer an obstacle to traffic but a place to stop and look back.

Epilogue · 製作幕後

Behind the Images

The four scenes on this page are AI-generated reconstructions, not historical photographs. They are meant to help readers imagine change over time, not to document exact details.

01

The Tool

All images were created with [AI tool name], a text-to-image generator.

Each image uses the same 16:9 frame (1672 × 941 px), so the four eras can be compared side by side.

02

The Process

I started with one base prompt that fixed the camera: the North Gate centered, seen head-on from street level, with a road leading through the arch.

For each era, I kept that description and changed only the period details, then picked the most convincing result out of [number] attempts.

03

Prompt Adjustments

[Base prompt] Taipei North Gate (Cheng'en Gate), centered, symmetrical, street-level view, red upper wall, grey stone base, arched passage, clear daylight

Era details added on top of the base prompt:

1920s · rickshaws, kimono 1950s · bicycles, old trucks 1990s · taxis, scooters 2020s · plaza, glass towers
04

Challenges

  • Text on signs. AI often draws Chinese and Japanese characters incorrectly, so every sign had to be checked.
  • Keeping the gate the same. Small changes in a prompt could move the camera or reshape the roof.
  • History vs. impression. AI draws what looks old, not what existed. The 1990s image leaves out the real elevated ramp.
